segments.arabic:
١١٩٩٢- أم حكيم بنت وداع:
ويقال بنت وادع الخزاعية» .
قال أبو نعيم: كانت من المهاجرات.
وقال أبو عمر: سمعت النبي ﵌ يقول: «عجّلوا الإفطار وأخّروا السّحور» «٢» .
روت عنها صفية بنت جرير.
قلت: وصله أبو يعلى،
وأخرجه ابن مندة، من طرق عن أبي سلمة موسى بن إسماعيل، عن حبابة بنت عجلان، عن أمها أم حفص، عن صفية، وساق بهذا الإسناد أحاديث أربعة أخر، منها: قالت قلت: للنّبيّ ﵌: رد اللطف؟
فقال: «ما أقبحه! لو أهدي إليّ كراع لقبلته، ولو دعيت إليه لأجبته» «٣» .
ومنها ما أخرجه ابن ماجة بهذا الإسناد، دعاء الوالد يفضي إلى الحجاب «٤» .
وأخرج ابن سعد عن موسى بهذا الإسناد حديث: ما جزاء الغني من الفقير؟ قال: النصيحة والدعاء.
وقال: روت أم حكيم أحاديث بهذا الإسناد.
segments.english:
11992—Umm Hakim bint Wada':

She is also said to be Umm Hakim bint Wadi' al-Khuza'iyya.[1]

Abu Nu'aym said: She was one of the female Emigrants.

Abu Umar said: She said, “I heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: ‘Hasten the breaking of the fast and delay the pre-dawn meal.’”[2]

Safiyya bint Jarir narrated from her.

I say: Abu Ya'la supplied its continuous chain, and Ibn Manda transmitted it through several routes from Abu Salama Musa ibn Isma'il, from Hababa bint Ajlan, from her mother Umm Hafs, from Safiyya. Through this isnad he related four other hadiths, among them her report: She said, “I said to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): ‘Should a gift be turned away?’ He replied: ‘How ugly that is! If a sheep’s trotter were given to me as a gift, I would accept it, and if I were invited to it, I would answer the invitation.’”[3]

Another is the report transmitted by Ibn Majah through this isnad: “A father’s supplication reaches the Veil.”[4]

Ibn Sa'd transmitted from Musa through this isnad the hadith: “What recompense is due to the wealthy from the poor?” He replied: “Sincere counsel and supplication.”

He said: Umm Hakim narrated several hadiths through this isnad.

names.english: Abu Salama Musa ibn Isma'il al-Tabudhaki

unresolved.explanation: The spelling is secure, but the unvocalized evidence cannot distinguish Wada' from Wadda'. The established provisional rendering Wada' has therefore been retained.
